## Summary

Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.

Add coverage for matching values in adoption mode and for existing keys in default mode. The current tests would miss a regression in whether those calls rewrite the configuration.

## Changes

The pull request adds an `adopt` flag that records incoming keys already present in the configuration, even when their values match. Replacement still records only differing values, and the merger writes the file when it records a change.

## Critical

(none)

## Important

- app/config.py:15 — tests — Cover adoption when values already match — With `adopt=True` and stored and incoming `theme` both set to `"dark"`, no test verifies that adoption records the key. `test_adopt_updates_setting` uses differing values, so it would still pass if adoption skipped matches. — A regression could omit matching keys from the returned change list and skip the write when those are the only keys supplied.
- app/config.py:18 — tests — Cover existing keys with both flags disabled — With a stored `theme` of `"light"` and an incoming value of `"dark"`, no test checks that the default merge preserves the stored setting. The only default-mode test starts with an empty configuration. — An accidental overwrite of existing user settings in default mode could pass the test suite.
